dedupe_keys.name: geospatial modelling of australia s national electricity market network and generator data set

description: This data set describes the topology of Australia's largest transmission network, the National Electricity Market, with the technical and economic characteristics of the generators connected to it. It was compiled by Aleksis Xenophon and David Hill from public data sets of the Australian Energy Market Operator (AEMO) and Geoscience Australia, for building economic dispatch, power flow and unit commitment models. The network has 912 nodes, 1,406 AC edges and three HVDC links, with forward and reverse flow limits for two AC interconnectors, and every node has latitude and longitude taken from Geoscience Australia geospatial data. Coverage is the eastern and southern Australian grid of the NEM at node level. Files are in a GitHub repository with versions archived on Zenodo (version 1.1 archive of about 1.4 MB, last commit August 2018) under CC-BY-4.0 at no cost. Caveats: the data reflect sources available in 2018, and electrical parameters of lines are approximations derived from public information, not operator data. Simulation uses are power flow, dispatch and market modelling of the Australian grid. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
